dēdecus, dēdecoris n.

noun, third declension

disgrace, dishonour, shame

Other words

  • ignōminia, ignōminiae f. — disgrace, public dishonour

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 151, 157; Traupman 304

    Properly the loss of one’s good name (nōmen), a mark of public disgrace.

  • dēdecorī esse (+ dative) — to be a disgrace to

    predicative dative with esse and the dative of the person · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.139: ampla domus dēdecorī saepe dominō fit (Lewis & Short s.v. sōlitūdō; s.v. dēdecus without saepe); Ter. Haut. 2.3.93: dēdecorī est (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151; Traupman 304

  • ignōminiōsus, ignōminiōsa, ignōminiōsum — disgraceful, shameful

    declension · also used · classical · Quint. 7.1.8 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151, 157

  • dēdecōrus, dēdecōra, dēdecōrum — disgraceful, dishonourable

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 5.2.73 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151

    Lewis & Short: very rare.

  • flāgitiōsus, flāgitiōsa, flāgitiōsum — scandalous, shameful

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 157

  • flāgitium, flāgitiī n. — a shameful deed, an outrage, a scandal; the disgrace of it

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 853: meōque fīliō sciente id facere flāgitium patrem?; Cic. Sen. 40: stupra et adulteria et omne tāle flāgitium (Lewis & Short)

    In comedy also of a person: flāgitium hominis, you disgrace of a man (Plaut. Asin. 473).

  • probrum, probrī n. — a shameful act; the shame of it; a reproach, an insult

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 477: atque īnsimulābit eam probrī; Sall. J. 44.5: ignāviae luxuriaeque probra (Lewis & Short)

  • turpitūdō, turpitūdinis f. — ugliness; baseness, shamefulness, disgrace

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 1.49: turpitūdinem atque īnfāmiam dēlēre ac tollere (Lewis & Short); Sall. Cat. 13.2 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Edepol facinus improbum est!

    That’s a darn disgrace!Traupman 305

  • Flāgitium hominis. Dā, obsecrō, argentum huic, nē male loquātur.

    You disgrace of a man! Give him the money, please, or he’ll start abusing us.Plaut. Asin. 473

  • turpitūdinem atque īnfāmiam dēlēre ac tollere

    to wipe out and remove the disgrace and the ill fameCic. Verr. 1.49 (Lewis & Short)

See also what a shame!.
